description.summary: tiling or floating, for the focused workspace

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a shell component, such as a bar, show whether the focused workspace arranges its windows in tiles or lets them float, and switch it between the two.
The mode belongs to a workspace, and each workspace keeps its own. The one this protocol reports and changes is the active workspace of the focused output: the workspace the compositor's own keyboard shortcut for the same switch acts on. Moving focus to a workspace in the other mode is reported like any other change.
Only privileged clients can bind the manager global. A compositor must not expose it to sandboxed clients.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_workspace_mode_manager_v1
interface.description: Reports the focused workspace's mode with a mode event as soon as the global is bound, and again every time it changes.

entry.name: tiling
entry.summary: windows tile the workspace without overlapping

entry.name: floating
entry.summary: windows keep their own size and place, and may overlap

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. The compositor sends no further events for it.

request.name: set_mode
request.description:
Switch the focused workspace to mode. Windows following the old mode are converted, and the compositor answers with a mode event once the workspace has switched. Asking for the mode the workspace is already in does nothing.
A value that names no mode is an invalid_mode protocol error.

event.name: mode
event.description: The mode of the focused workspace, sent once right after binding and again whenever it changes, whether the workspace switched or focus moved to a workspace in the other mode.
